title: Modern No-Code AI Route : AI Generalist to AI Builder
_comment_overview: PARAPHRASED from the krishnaik.in landing page — never copy marketing prose verbatim. Facts (fee, dates, schedule, tool names, project list) are used as-is.
overview: A live, mentor-led program that takes beginners and working professionals from foundational AI concepts to building real AI-powered products without writing code. It covers AI assistant mastery, prompt engineering, content and data-storytelling systems, no-code app development with Lovable, Bolt.new and v0 by Vercel, and workflow automation with Zapier, Make and n8n AI agents. Runs Saturday and Sunday evenings (IST) and closes with two capstone projects: a deployed no-code AI application and an automation system.
_comment_category: Primary category reflects the course's core: applying generative AI assistants and tools end to end. 'Agentic AI' is secondary for the n8n AI Agent module (module group 11); 'Analytics' is secondary for the data-storytelling/dashboard module (group 6).
_comment_level: Page markets explicitly to 'first-time AI users' and 'non-technical' audiences with no prerequisites, so beginner is the honest fusion anchor. level_range extends to intermediate because the automation/AI-agent modules (Zapier/Make workflow design, n8n AI Agent construction) require more structured technical thinking than the earlier prompt/assistant modules — stored only, not scored per schema §1.
_comment_price: ₹7500.00 stated inclusive of GST on the own-site landing page (fixed price, not coupon-driven), so a number is safe here. price_band 'mid' per schema §2 (₹3,000–₹9,999).
_comment_rating: No rating or review count published on the landing page. Left null rather than guessed — the validator's null-rating warning is expected.

format._comment_cohort_start: Landing page states 'Start Date: May 17, 2026', but curation date is 2026-08-06 — that cohort has already begun, so per schema §3 it CANNOT live in format.cohort_start (generate would wrongly tell a user today to enrol for a cohort that already started). Moved to top-level cohort_start_stale instead. No next-cohort date is published, so cohort_start is left null; per §6 this demotes the freshness mode prior from 'live' (1.00) to the 'recorded' prior (0.45) until a future cohort_start is captured.
format._comment_enrollment_status: Page still shows active 'Enroll Now' CTAs and a stated fee despite the started cohort — read as open enrollment (likely joining the running batch or a rolling next batch), not confirmed closed/waitlisted.
format._comment_duration: Two figures on the page: the overview header says '3 Months', the mentor bio block says '3-4 months'. Stored the mentor-block figure as the more detailed/conservative one; the gap is listing inconsistency, not a version skew.
format._comment_recording: Page explicitly grants 'Access To 1.0 AI For Everyone Batch recordings' (a prior cohort) as a bonus perk, and offers 1.5-year dashboard access — taken together this implies session recordings are part of the delivery model, though the page does not explicitly confirm THIS batch's own live sessions are recorded for later viewing.
format._comment_curriculum_version: No version string published for this batch. Null per §7 rather than inventing one.

_comment_objectives: §1 corroboration rule applied. Each objective maps to a real module_groups cluster below: (1)->foundations+assistants, (2)->prompt engineering, (3)->research & productivity, (4)->writing+presentations, (5)->image+video, (6)->no-code apps, (7)->automation+n8n, (8)->strategy. Nothing published was dropped.
_comment_modules: VERSION/UI SKEW noted. The full curriculum body on the page describes 12 thematic sections (Foundations, Assistants, Prompt Engineering, Research, Writing, Presentations & Data Storytelling, Image, Video, No-Code Apps, Automation Foundations, Advanced Automation/n8n, Strategy). A separate numbered tab/footer element on the same page lists only 10 names, omitting 'AI Presentations & Data Storytelling' and 'Automation Foundations (Zapier & Make)' — almost certainly a UI tab-count artifact, not a real 10-vs-12 curriculum difference, since both missing sections are fully described in the body copy with real tool names. The 12-section body is treated as authoritative. Source page publishes no itemized lecture list per section, only paragraph descriptions naming specific tools/techniques — the module bullets below extract those named facts (tool names, concrete techniques), not paraphrase.

_comment_skills: 39 entries exceeds the schema's 30-item guidance, which is a real signal here rather than a slip: the page itself advertises '40+ industry-leading tools' across four learning tracks (assistants, content, no-code apps, automation). Kept in full since each is a genuine named tool a user might search for.
